title: Groupe de Galois motivique : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 26-28). Fix k ⊂ C and a Tannakian category M of (possibly mixed) motives over k with two fibre functors. T_B is the Betti functor to Q-vector spaces, enriched with a Hodge structure. T_DR is the de Rham functor to k-vector spaces, with its Hodge filtration. Let G = Aut⊗(T_B), the motivic Galois group. Then P = Isom⊗(T_B⊗k, T_DR) is a G_k-torsor (the period torsor), and the comparison isomorphism gives a point φ ∈ P(C). Write G' = ad(P) = Aut⊗(T_DR). Let H' ⊂ G' be the automorphisms of T_DR that respect the Hodge filtration and act trivially on gr.

This page adds the Hodge filtration in group-theoretic terms.
(9) H' is unipotent. Let T_Hdg = gr_F T_DR, a graded (bigraded) fibre functor over k. Then Q = Isom⊗(T_DR, T_Hdg), restricted to isomorphisms inducing the identity on gr, is a right H'-torsor. In modern terms, Q is the scheme of tensor-compatible splittings of the Hodge filtration.
(10)-(11) Twisting by Q transports groups to the graded side:
- H'' = Q ×^{H'} H' = ad(H'). This is the subgroup of G'' = Aut⊗(T_Hdg) preserving the filtration attached to the grading and trivial on the associated graded.
- G'' = Q ×^{H'} G' = Aut⊗(T_Hdg).
(12)-(13) The bigrading of T_Hdg by (p, q = w − p) gives two cocharacters i_1, i_2 : G_{m,k} → G'' (written G' on the page; they agree since Q is trivial). Here i : G_m → G is the weight cocharacter and ε : G → G_m is the Tate character. The cocharacters satisfy ε∘i_1 = ε∘i_2 = id and i_1·i_2 = i, so ε∘i = λ².

The page then lists the abstract data that should classify such a motivic category:
(a) G over Q with G_m →i G →ε G_m.
(b) G'' over k with i'', ε''.
(c) i_1, i_2 satisfying (13).
(d) A left torsor Q under the unipotent H'' ⊂ G''. H'' is determined by i_1: it is the unipotent group U_{μ} of the filtration defined by a cocharacter. From Q one recovers H' = ad(Q), P := G'' ×^{H''} Q and G' = ad_{G''}(Q). NB: Q is trivial (unipotent group in characteristic 0), so G' ≅ G''.
(e) A left torsor P under G'.
(f) An identification G⊗_Q k ≅ ad_{G'}(P), compatible with i and ε.
(g) A point φ ∈ P(C).

The next page imposes conditions so that these data come from motives: the induced filtrations give Hodge structures; a 'multiplicative' condition; compatibility with restriction of scalars. Grothendieck admits he cannot express conditions 2) and 3) directly in terms of the data.

Overall this is an early Tannakian 'Hodge-de Rham-Betti datum': the motivic Galois group, the period torsor with its comparison point, and the Hodge filtration encoded by a cocharacter defined over k on the de Rham side. Its purpose is to describe M ≈ Rep(G), assuming the Hodge conjecture.
errors: (12): the cocharacters land in G'' = Aut⊗(T_Hdg), as corrected on the next page. Writing G' is harmless only because Q is trivial, so G' ≅ G''.
(10): H'' is described as a subgroup of 'H''' where G'' = Aut⊗(T_Hdg) is meant. The contracted product should be Q ×^{H'} H' (the transcription gives H).
(d): the formula H' = H'' ×^{H''} Q is notationally garbled. What is meant is that H' = ad(Q) when Q is viewed as an (H',H'')-bitorsor, as made explicit on the next page.
Q is first called a right H'-torsor and later a left H''-torsor. It is really a bitorsor (made explicit on p.28).
Triviality of Q uses H^1(k, U) = 0 for unipotent U in characteristic 0. This is correct for k ⊂ C but left unjustified.
The 'bigrading' of gr_F T_DR by (p, w−p) needs the weight grading. For mixed motives one needs gr_F gr_W, which is not addressed here.

ideas.what: Motivic Galois group G = Aut⊗(T_B), de Rham functor as a twist T_DR = P ×^G (T_B⊗k), and comparison point φ ∈ P(C)
ideas.modern_name: Period torsor / Tannakian torsor of periods
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (1960s, via Saavedra 1972); developed by Deligne, Kontsevich–Zagier, André
ideas.where_published: Footnote on periods in 'On the de Rham cohomology of algebraic varieties' (1966); Saavedra Rivano, Catégories tannakiennes (1972)

ideas.what: The Hodge filtration on the de Rham fibre functor encoded by the unipotent group H' and the torsor Q of tensor splittings; Q is trivial because H' is unipotent
ideas.modern_name: Filtered fibre functors; splitting of ⊗-filtrations; U_μ attached to a cocharacter
ideas.usually_credited_to: Saavedra Rivano (1972), Deligne; Ziegler for splitting of filtered fibre functors

ideas.what: Hodge bigrading as two cocharacters i_1, i_2 defined over k, with ε∘i_j = id and i_1 i_2 = i (weight)
ideas.modern_name: Hodge cocharacter μ (and its conjugate) and the weight cocharacter, as in Mumford–Tate / Shimura datum formalism
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (Travaux de Shimura 1971; Variétés de Shimura 1979), Saavedra

ideas.what: A list of abstract data (a)–(g) intended to classify a category of motives over k ⊂ C, assuming the Hodge conjecture
ideas.modern_name: Tannakian description of motives / mixed-realization data (Betti, de Rham, comparison, Hodge filtration)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (Hodge cycles 1982; Le groupe fondamental de la droite projective 1989), Jannsen (mixed realizations)

missed.claim: Grothendieck tries to characterise which group-theoretic data (G, P, φ, i_1, i_2, Q) come from motives. He finds he cannot express the needed conditions (Hodge-type, 'multiplicative', restriction-of-scalars compatibility) intrinsically in terms of the data. This is an early form of the still-open problem of characterising motivic period structures among abstract Hodge–de Rham–Betti data.
missed.quote: Ainsi, on obtient les données suivantes a) Groupe algébrique G sur Q ... g) Un élément φ ∈ P(C)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This relates to characterising the image of motives in Hodge-de Rham-Betti realizations: Hodge, Tate and period conjectures, and André's motivated motives. It is historically notable as a 1965 formulation with the Hodge cocharacter defined over k.

missed.claim: By 1965 Grothendieck was already encoding the Hodge filtration by cocharacters and a unipotent splitting torsor inside the Tannakian group of the de Rham fibre functor over k. This predates the published Saavedra/Deligne formalism of filtered fibre functors and Hodge cocharacters.
missed.quote: Q = Isom_{⊗, ind. l'identité sur gradué}(T_DR, T_Hdg) ... i_1, i_2 : G_{m,k} → G'
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a priority and history detail for the cocharacter (Mumford–Tate / Shimura-datum style) formalism. It is not new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: Grothendieck's period-torsor viewpoint is known through Saavedra and André. The explicit 1965 treatment of the Hodge filtration via over-k cocharacters and a unipotent splitting torsor is a notable unpublished anticipation of Deligne-style formalism. It is not mathematically new today.
transcription_corrections: f) should read 'G ⊗_Q k ≃ G' ×^{G'} P = ad_{G'}(P)', not '⊗_R'.

(10): 'H'' = Q ×^{H'} H'' (superscript H'), i.e. ad(H'), described as the 'sous-groupe de G'' = Aut⊗(T_Hdg) respectant la filtration associée à la bigraduation, et induisant l'identité sur gradué associé'.
In the margin, an arrow from 'Posons' links to (10) and (11); the right-hand text belongs to (10).
d): 'Torseur à g.' means 'torseur à gauche'. The insertion reads 'H'' unipotent ⊂ G''', with 'défini par' i_1 implied.
